tasks.build:all: deno task build:release && deno task build:ffi && deno task build:packages && deno task build:napi:packages
tasks.build:packages: deno task build:npm:format && deno task build:wasm:deno && deno task build:npm:parse && deno task build:wasm:parse:deno && deno task build:npm:all && deno task build:wasm:all:deno
tasks.build:ffi:format: deno task build:stamped -p tsv_ffi --release --no-default-features --features format --target-dir target/ffi-format
tasks.build:ffi:parse: deno task build:stamped -p tsv_ffi --release --no-default-features --features parse --target-dir target/ffi-parse
tasks.build:ffi:all: deno task build:ffi && deno task build:ffi:format && deno task build:ffi:parse

tasks.//build:bench: Everything a bench leg measures or sizes: the profile-guided native pair every timed native row loads (`build:bench:pgo`), the two size-only FFI subset builds, which stay plain (no row executes them, and each would need a training of its own — a profile applies only to the feature set it was trained at), and the wasm bundles (never profile-guided).
tasks.build:bench: deno task build:bench:pgo && deno task build:bench:deno && deno task build:bench:node
tasks.build:bench:deno: deno task build:ffi:format && deno task build:ffi:parse && deno task build:wasm:deno && deno task build:wasm:parse:deno && deno task build:wasm:all:deno
tasks.//typecheck:js: Typechecks the JS/TS the repo owns that the bench harness and scripts/ run, which `deno task typecheck` (cargo) does not see, in two programs. First `tsc -p tsconfig.bench.json`, the bench entries that run under Node (every root under `benches/js/roots/`, a glob, so a new root is covered the day it appears) and what each imports, with Node's types and no `Deno` global; their packages resolve from benches/js/node_modules, `@fuzdev/gro` from the root install above it. Then `deno check` under the bench config, directory arguments, not per-directory globs: deno walks them (skipping node_modules) so a new subdirectory is covered the day it appears, where a glob list silently is not; the walk takes in the Node roots too, resolving their `@fuzdev/gro` from the root install. NOT in `deno task check`: the harness imports npm packages by bare specifier, so this needs `deno task bench:install`, and CI's check job deliberately installs no bench node_modules (.github/workflows/check.yml). The node-modules-free halves are carved out into typecheck:scripts and typecheck:bench-core, which DO gate — so what only this task covers is the npm-importing part of benches/js (the impl wrappers and the entry points that import packages). The tsv_debug sidecar runs on Node and is typechecked by `typecheck:scripts`' `tsc` program. Same posture as test:node:canonical — run it after a harness or scripts change.
tasks.typecheck:js: node node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.bench.json && deno check --config benches/js/deno.json benches/js scripts
tasks.//typecheck:scripts: Typechecks scripts/ in two programs, each by the checker of the runtime its files run on, so it CAN gate in `check`: nothing else typechecks the release scripts, and `deno run` does not — so publish.ts / publish_napi.ts / build_napi_packages.ts, whose first real execution is a release, would otherwise reach it unchecked. First `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json`, the scripts that run under Node: every root under `scripts/roots/` (a glob, so a new root is covered the day it appears) and what it imports, with Node's types and no `Deno` global, plus the PGO pipeline (`scripts/pgo/pgo.ts`) and the drivers it runs with `node` (`scripts/pgo/addon_ops.ts`, `scripts/pgo/addon_depth.ts`), whose release rows on Windows run them with no install, the bench entries that run under Node and need no bench package (`benches/js/roots/divergence_audit.ts`, `benches/js/roots/corpus_stats.ts`, `benches/js/roots/compose_reports.ts`, named, since the rest of `benches/js/roots/` needs the bench install, and held to the list by a row of `scripts/no_package_closure_test.ts`, which fails on a root that loads no bench package and is not named), so they and their libraries gate where `typecheck:js` cannot, and tsv_debug's sidecar (`crates/tsv_debug/sidecar/sidecar.ts`), whose packages resolve from its own install, so this half needs `npm ci --prefix crates/tsv_debug/sidecar` as well as the root's `npm ci`. Then `deno check` over the scripts Deno still runs, a DIRECTORY walk (a new script is covered the day it appears, where a file list silently is not) minus what the root config's `exclude` names: the Node scripts and their libraries, which import `@fuzdev/gro` and so cannot resolve here; the entries CI runs with no `node_modules` (on Windows too: `build:stamped`'s, `build:napi:packages`' staging, `validate:napi`'s, the PGO pipeline's; in the credentialed release jobs: `publish:napi`'s, `release:notes`', `release:assets`') and their libraries are in both halves, since they must import no package. That half is node-modules-free by construction, which is what lets it run on a checkout with no `node_modules`: every module it reaches resolves to relative paths and node: builtins. `--no-lock`: the repo is deliberately deno.lock-free. `DENO_NO_PACKAGE_JSON=1`: with the root package.json in view, Deno resolves a bare specifier through the node_modules npm installs from it, any package there, so a script's bare import would typecheck here and fail at its first real run.
tasks.typecheck:scripts: node node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json && DENO_NO_PACKAGE_JSON=1 deno check --no-lock scripts
tasks.//build:check: The ONE `--profile corpus` build world every `deno task check` audit leg shares, built in ONE cargo invocation so the stack compiles once. The `tsv_debug` legs select `-p tsv_debug --features _internal_audits`; the two `tsv_cli` ones (`format:audit`, `discovery:audit`) need the `tsv` BINARY, which that selection builds only as a library dependency — and `-p tsv_cli` ALONE resolves features without `_internal_audits`, so it was a second, fully duplicated compile of `tsv_lang` → `tsv_ts`/`tsv_css`/`tsv_svelte`/`tsv_cli` in the same profile (20.5 s of the 30.4 s stack, on every edit; `ls target/corpus/.fingerprint | grep tsv_lang` showed the duplicate). Selecting BOTH packages in one invocation collapses them: `tsv_debug` depends on `tsv_cli`, so adding `tsv_cli` to the selection adds no feature the unified graph did not already carry, and a following `cargo run -p tsv_debug --features _internal_audits` is a 0.04 s no-op re-check rather than a rebuild. The legs therefore keep their own `cargo run` — freshness per leg, one world. ⚠ The `tsv` binary this builds carries the ledger / swallow seams COMPILED IN (inert until armed, so `format --check` is byte-identical), which is exactly why no perf task may measure it: `profile`, `bench` and the release artifacts build their own default-feature worlds and must keep doing so.
tasks.build:check: deno task build:stamped --profile corpus -p tsv_cli -p tsv_debug --features tsv_debug/_internal_audits --quiet
tasks.check: cargo fmt --check && deno task format:audit && deno task pins:audit && deno task docs:audit && deno task docs:audit:docsrs && deno task deps:audit && deno task package:audit && deno task typecheck && deno task typecheck:features && deno task typecheck:scripts && deno task typecheck:bench-core && deno task conformance:audit && deno task conformance:audit:compiler && deno task variants:audit && deno task scan:audit && deno task fanout:audit && deno task roundtrip:audit && deno task roundtrip:audit:prettier && deno task discovery:audit && deno task canonicalize:audit && deno task binding:audit && deno task authoring:audit && deno task paren:audit && deno task razor:audit && deno task fuzz:audit && deno task fuzz:audit:debug && deno task test:node && deno task test:deno && deno task test && deno task test:depth && deno task test:audits && deno task swallow:audit && deno task comments:audit && deno task gaps:audit && deno task blanks:audit && deno task fabrication:audit && deno task census:audit && deno task width:audit && deno task ignore:audit && deno task check:ast-types && deno task check:loc && deno task lint
tasks.//check:loc: The `loc` CROSS-GRADE: tsv's two implementations of one `loc` definition — the Rust writers' loc wire and the shipped `crates/tsv_wasm/npm/locations.js` reconstruction of the span-only wire — deep-equal (key order ignored) over every parseable fixture document — each input and its format variants, which need no oracle (a prettier-side form tsv rejects is counted, not failed; `loc_wires`' module doc). The fixtures pin the span-only wire, so this is the only `check` leg that grades `loc`; its outside reference (acorn / Svelte) is `corpus:compare:parse`'s loc arm, at conformance cadence. One `tsv_debug loc_wires` process streams both wires as NDJSON, so it needs no sidecar and no node_modules. See docs/audits.md §Loc Cross-Grade.
tasks.//strip:corpus: The type strip's CORPUS differential (benches/js/strip_corpus.ts): tsv_ts::strip against ts-blank-space over the strippable TypeScript of the `gates` view's snapshot tiers, failing on a panic, a contract or idempotence finding, an output that is no JS module, a byte or refusal disagreement outside its reviewed ACCEPTED list, a stale entry, or a count off STRIP_CORPUS_PINS. Reads ../corpora and node_modules, so it is NOT in `check`; a `conformance` leg. tsv's side is one `target/corpus/tsv_debug strip --stdin` process, hence `build:check`; `strip:corpus:run`, the npm script that runs the differential under Node (docs/tasks.md §`strip:corpus:run`), skips the build (freshness-guarded).
tasks.strip:corpus: deno task build:check && deno task strip:corpus:run
tasks.//imports:corpus: The import records' CORPUS differential (benches/js/imports_corpus.ts): tsv_ts::parse_imports / tsv_svelte::parse_imports against oxc-parser's module record over the JS/TS-family files and Svelte components of the `gates` view's snapshot tiers (a component's scripts found by svelte/compiler), every structural difference between the two models a named normalization, failing on a panic, a parse error on either side, a record or hasModuleSyntax difference outside its reviewed ACCEPTED list, a stale entry, or a count off IMPORTS_CORPUS_PINS. Reads ../corpora and node_modules, so it is NOT in `check`; a `conformance` leg. tsv's side is one `target/corpus/tsv_debug imports --stdin` process, hence `build:check`; `imports:corpus:run`, the npm script that runs the differential under Node (docs/tasks.md §`imports:corpus:run`), skips the build (freshness-guarded).
tasks.imports:corpus: deno task build:check && deno task imports:corpus:run
tasks.fuzz:audit: cargo run --profile corpus -p tsv_debug --features _internal_audits --quiet fuzz --seed 0 --iterations 5000 && deno task fuzz:audit:css && deno task fuzz:audit:ts
tasks.//perf:ab: Parse / format performance A/B between two trees per language (TS, Svelte, CSS), plus the type strip: wall-clock medians plus `instructions:u` from `perf stat`, exit 1 when a row regresses. Builds each side from a git snapshot of its build inputs in `~/.cache/tsv/perf_ab/` (keyed by a hash of the build inputs' `git ls-tree -r -z` entries minus the overlaid drivers, so a tests- or docs-only change reuses the binary, and each binary by its driver's content and the build recipe, so a recipe change rebuilds; the most recently used few kept) with the current `crates/tsv_debug/examples/perf_ab.rs` and `perf_ab_strip.rs` drivers overlaid (a tree without the type strip builds only the first, and the run skips the strip rows loudly), in a cleared environment — the `--allow-env` list is exactly what a build keeps (toolchain lookup + `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`), so a caller's `RUSTFLAGS` / `CARGO_PROFILE_*` cannot reach one side's build. The candidate defaults to the working tree. Broad `--allow-run`: the driver binaries live at cache paths no allow-list can name ahead of time; `--allow-write` bounds the script's own writes only (child processes are not held to it — the working-tree snapshot writes loose objects into the repo's object store). NOT in `check` — it builds two release trees. Rule + rationale: docs/performance.md §Gating a change against a base.
tasks.//branch:report: One document comparing two refs on every axis a merge read needs (sizes, type widths, work counters, recursion depth; build wall and timing behind --timing; see scripts/branch_report/branch_report.ts). Builds each ref from git in its own tree and target dir under ~/.cache/tsv/branch_report, and writes report.md + report.json. The same ref on both sides is the A/A null, whose JSON is the floor for later timing rows (--aa). A missing tool, skip or failed build is reported and exits non-zero unless --accept-gaps. NOT in `check` — it builds two release trees.
tasks.//bench: The full refresh, and the one caller that composes TWICE — deliberately. `bench:perf` ends with `bench:compose` so it stands alone, but compose reads `report.conformance.node.json` for the combined report's `conformance_vintage`, and `bench:conformance` rewrites that file AFTER it. Without the trailing compose the combined report a full run publishes describes the PREVIOUS conformance run — stamping `stale: true` and an older commit at the exact moment both halves were just refreshed at the same one, and naming the wrong half in the remedy. The re-run reads four JSON files and writes two; the alternative (moving compose out of `bench:perf`, or chaining it onto `bench:conformance`) breaks a perf-only or conformance-only machine.
tasks.bench: deno task bench:perf && deno task bench:conformance && deno task bench:compose
tasks.//bench:perf: Builds the whole artifact set ONCE, then measures it under each runtime with the `:run` legs (freshness-guarded, so the order is provable rather than assumed). Chains `bench:harvest:svelte-styles` and NOT the suite harvests: the corpus VIEWS decide who needs which cache, and the perf view holds only the `benched` svelte_styles cache (benches/js/CLAUDE.md §Harvests).
tasks.bench:perf: deno task bench:runtimes && deno task bench:harvest:svelte-styles && deno task build:bench && deno task bench:deno:run && deno task bench:node:run && deno task bench:bun:run && deno task bench:compose
tasks.//bench:deno: Every standalone per-runtime leg (`bench:deno` / `bench:node` / `bench:bun`, and `bench:conformance`) builds the WHOLE artifact set, not its own half. Each leg REPORTS the same tsv binary-size rows, cross-binding by design: `binary_sizes.ts` sizes the tsv artifacts by PATH rather than by the impl registry, so the deno report carries `tsv (napi)` and the node/bun reports the `tsv (ffi)` trio. Built per half, a leg would size the other half at whatever commit it was last built while sizing its own at HEAD, inside sibling reports all stamped with one `git_commit`. `lib/check_artifact_freshness.ts` warns when a `:run` leg is about to do exactly that (`warn_stale_reported_artifacts`); building everything is what makes the warning unreachable here. Warm, the other half costs about a second (`run_if_stale` skips each wasm-pack, cargo no-ops, `build:bench:pgo` skips on a current stamp).
tasks.bench:deno: deno task build:bench && deno task bench:deno:run
tasks.//rsvelte-allow-run: The rsvelte-fmt row spawns a prebuilt binary (it ships no in-process API — see benches/js/lib/rsvelte.ts), so `smoke` must permit it by path (a bench run's pre-flight child is granted the one installed binary by `benches/js/lib/bench_child.ts`). All five published platform packages are listed because the task string is static while the installed one is per-machine; Deno ignores a nonexistent path entry silently (unlike a bare NAME, which logs a resolution failure), so the four that don't apply cost nothing. Node and Bun need no equivalent.
tasks.//bench:deno:run: The ORCHESTRATOR's permissions only. A bench run is several processes (benches/js/bench.ts §Process model): this one loads no engine and no corpus — it starts the pre-flight process and one process per timed row per pass, and writes the report — so it asks for read, write to the results directory, and to run `deno` (its children) and `git` (the report's commit). What the children may do (FFI, the rsvelte-fmt binary, gzip, net) is stated once, in benches/js/lib/bench_child.ts, since Deno hands a child none of its parent's permissions. `--v8-flags=--expose-gc` is passed on to the children, which is where it is used.
tasks.bench:node: deno task build:bench && deno task bench:node:run
tasks.bench:bun: deno task build:bench && deno task bench:bun:run
tasks.bench:conformance: deno task bench:pins:suites && deno task build:bench && deno task bench:conformance:run
tasks.//bench:harvest: Two groups, split because their consumers differ (benches/js/CLAUDE.md §Harvests is the full argument). `bench:pins:suites` is the conformance-view group: the five SUITE caches (wpt / test262 / ts-repo / svelte-rejects / prettier-jsx) plus the CSS reject PIN, which harvests nothing but is stamped and graded the same way — all `--if-present`, so each warn-skips an input it cannot see, which is what lets the group preflight `conformance` on a partial machine. WHAT it cannot see is the corpus loader's call, not each leg's: the two reject pins and the prettier-jsx harvest load through `load_pinned_language_corpus`, whose `{ complete_for: <language> }` policy refuses an absent entry that could hold that language (`optional` ones INCLUDED — `optional` says only that an ordinary run may proceed without it, never that a pinned count still describes the corpus) and waves through one that cannot. Spelling that tolerance as a plain allow-missing instead is the bug the policy exists to prevent (benches/js/CLAUDE.md §Harvests). `bench:harvest:svelte-styles` is the perf-view group of one: stamped on the ../corpora `collections/` tree id + its EXACT block pin + the perf view's entry list (skips instantly when none moved), and it FAILS rather than warn-skips on a missing snapshot collection. This task stays the manual refresh-everything entry point.
tasks.bench:harvest: deno task bench:pins:suites && deno task bench:harvest:svelte-styles
tasks.bench:pins:suites: deno task bench:harvest:wpt && deno task bench:harvest:test262 && deno task bench:harvest:ts-repo && deno task bench:harvest:svelte-rejects && deno task bench:harvest:prettier-jsx && deno task css:over-acceptance:pin
tasks.corpus:compare:parse: deno task build:napi:corpus && deno task build:check && deno task corpus:compare:parse:run
tasks.//wire:audit: The WIRE-INJECTION audit: the parse-side sibling of gaps/blanks — those inject into a fixture and grade the FORMATTER, this injects whitespace into every Svelte tag/block head and grades the resulting WIRE against the canonical parser (benches/js/lib/wire_inject.ts). Runs as a CENSUS (`--inject-limit 0`, every site), since a sample cannot be ratcheted. Green, but not in `check`: it needs the canonical parser, so conformance-tier. `wire:audit:terminators` is the lone CR / U+2028 / U+2029 family — document-wide, so a strided SAMPLE that cannot be ratcheted either, and ⚠️ RED BY DESIGN, like compile:fuzz. Model, coverage, blind spots: docs/audits.md §Wire-Injection Audit.
tasks.css:over-acceptance: deno task build:ffi:corpus && deno task build:wasm:all:deno && deno task css:over-acceptance:run
tasks.//css:over-acceptance:pin: The PIN alone — oracle only, no FFI/WASM build, freshness-stamped like the suite harvests, `--if-present` like them — so `bench:pins:suites` can carry `CSS_REJECTS_PIN` on the same cadence as its siblings instead of leaving it to a hand run (the one pin that once had no cadence at all). `--force` re-grades past a fresh stamp.
tasks.ts-repo:over-acceptance: deno task build:ffi:corpus && deno task build:wasm:all:deno && deno task ts-repo:over-acceptance:run
tasks.//conformance: The sidecar-cadence aggregate. `fixtures:validate` and `compile:fixtures:validate` preflight it as the ORACLE-FRESHNESS legs: `deno task check` runs each fixture tree's sidecar-free slice via cargo test, which grades tsv against the COMMITTED `output_prettier.*` / `expected_server.js` and so stays green when tsv and the committed file drift away from the live oracle together. Only a run that re-formats through prettier itself can see that — 17 s for all 4307 parser/formatter fixtures, which is why it gates here rather than living in a command someone has to remember. It cannot gate in `check`: that job runs on a bare CI checkout with no npm install, and the sidecar resolves its oracles from npm. `bench:pins:suites` preflights ahead of them as the PIN-FRESHNESS leg: the conformance-view count pins it re-derives are graded by no other cadence (docs/gate_counts.md §Where the numbers live), and it is ordered after `pins:audit:checkouts` (which names the checkout that moved) and before the fixture legs, so a corpus move is reported before anything expensive runs — seconds when nothing moved, and each leg warn-skips an absent checkout so a partial machine still reaches the legs below. `bench:harvest:svelte-styles` runs later, beside the corpus legs that read its cache: it loads the PERF view, where every ../corpora snapshot collection is REQUIRED, so it fails rather than warn-skips — the same requirement `corpus:compare` imposes a step later (benches/js/CLAUDE.md §Harvests). `strip:corpus:run` follows `build:check`, whose `tsv_debug` it drives: the type strip's differential against ts-blank-space, its own process since it asks nothing of the N-API addon or the canonical oracles (seconds); `imports:corpus:run` follows it on the same footing, the import records' differential against oxc-parser's module record. The driver runs under Node (`benches/js/roots/conformance.ts`, docs/tasks.md §`conformance`) and loads tsv's N-API addon at the `corpus` profile, which `build:napi:corpus` builds.
tasks.conformance: deno task pins:audit:checkouts && deno task bench:pins:suites && deno task fixtures:validate && deno task compile:fixtures:validate && deno task bench:harvest:svelte-styles && deno task build:napi:corpus && deno task build:check && deno task strip:corpus:run && deno task imports:corpus:run && PRETTIER_DEBUG=1 node benches/js/roots/conformance.ts
tasks.conformance:all: deno task conformance:test262 && deno task conformance
tasks.//test:deno: The suites still on `deno test`, the ones whose module under test calls `Deno.*` in the paths they test, so they gate in `deno task check` beside `test:node` (vitest under Node, which runs the rest; docs/tasks.md §`test:node`): `scripts/perf_ab_test.ts`, perf:ab's tree listing and its strip entry-point probe against a scratch git repo, with `scripts/branch_report/side_test.ts`, the branch report's corpus identity over one — tests that spawn a process and write, so they run with `--allow-read --allow-write --allow-run=git`, plus `--allow-env` for exactly the three variables that point git at another repo (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`), which perf_ab_test.ts clears so a run under a git hook cannot write the outer repo's index. Named paths, so a new Deno suite has to be added by name. It runs with `DENO_NO_PACKAGE_JSON=1`, so the root package.json and the node_modules npm installs from it stay out of their resolution, as in `typecheck:scripts`, and a bare import still fails them; and with `--no-config`, because the root config's `exclude` drops every `scripts/**/*_test.ts` from Deno's walks (see //exclude) and would drop these named ones too.
tasks.test:npm: deno task build:npm:format && deno task test:npm:run
tasks.//test:npm:run: The three wasm package suites' `:run` tasks have a SECOND spelling: scripts/publish.ts Step 6 runs `node --test scripts/test_npm.ts` per package itself (its own `PKG_DIR` loop, then `test:bun` once over all three with `--require-bun`) rather than calling these tasks. A leg added to one of them here is therefore NOT run by a publish until publish.ts gains it too — change both together.
tasks.test:npm:run: PKG_DIR=crates/tsv_wasm/pkg/format/npm node --test scripts/test_npm.ts && deno task test:bun format
tasks.test:npm:parse: deno task build:npm:parse && deno task test:npm:parse:run
tasks.test:npm:parse:run: PKG_DIR=crates/tsv_wasm/pkg/parse/npm node --test scripts/test_npm.ts && deno task test:bun parse
tasks.test:npm:all: deno task build:npm:all && deno task test:npm:all:run
tasks.test:npm:all:run: PKG_DIR=crates/tsv_wasm/pkg/all/npm node --test scripts/test_npm.ts && deno task test:bun all
tasks.test:napi: deno task build:napi:probe && deno task test:napi:run
tasks.test:napi:npm: deno task build:napi:packages && deno task test:napi:npm:run
tasks.test:napi:npm:run: node --test scripts/test_napi_npm.ts && deno task test:bun napi
tasks.//publish: The release driver, a Node script, and the one task here that runs no Deno: docs/tasks.md §`publish` says why it stays in deno.json.

//exclude: `scripts/**/*_test.ts` is out of the root config's walks because most of those suites run under vitest and import it, which `typecheck:scripts` cannot resolve: `tsc -p tsconfig.vitest.json` (in `test:node`) typechecks the vitest suites, and `deno test` typechecks the ones still its own, which `test:deno` names under `--no-config`. The rest are the scripts that run under Node over `@fuzdev/gro`'s host modules, which this walk cannot resolve: `scripts/roots` (a new root is out of the walk the day it appears) and, by name, each library a root imports that imports `@fuzdev/gro` itself, even as a type, so a new such library joins this list or the walk fails on its import. `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json`, `typecheck:scripts`' other half, checks them all (see //typecheck:scripts). The `!scripts/roots/…` names put back in the walk the entries CI runs with no `node_modules` (on Windows too: `build:stamped`'s, `build:napi:packages`' staging, `validate:napi`'s; in the credentialed release jobs: `publish:napi`'s, `release:notes`', `release:assets`'): each and its library import no package (docs/tasks.md §`build:stamped`, §`build:napi:packages`, §`validate:napi`, §`publish:napi`, §`release:notes`, §`release:assets`), and this walk, which resolves no package, is what holds them to it.
